<figcaption><strong>Drift plus control.</strong> At every state, the model's motion is a passive drift (blue) plus a push from the declared input (orange). Dashed: the same model with zero torque. Illustrative values from the pendulum model in <code>src/tangent_models/examples.py</code>; not a golfer measurement.</figcaption>
<details id="dpc-long">
<summary>Long description</summary>
<p>The horizontal axis is the pendulum angle from straight down, in radians; the vertical axis is its angular velocity, in radians per second. Faint arrows show the drift: the direction the model's state moves at each point with no torque. Both runs start at rest at an angle of -2.2 rad. The dashed curve is the zero-torque run, which follows the drift alone. The solid curve is the run under a constant 5 N m pivot torque, which swings faster and further. At the marked state, angle -1.94 rad and angular velocity 2.68 rad/s, three arrows show the change over 0.35 s: the drift arrow (2.68, 9.16) per second, the push arrow (0, 5.00) per second, which only changes angular velocity because torque acts on acceleration, and their sum, the state velocity the run actually has.</p>
</details>
</figure>
